Energy Security: Sulfur TES enables increased penetration of domestic renewable solar resources and reduces domestic consumption of natural gas for industrial heat, thus strengthening the nation's energy security. The planned product development activities include corrosion and mechanical durability testing to identify feasible materials that are compatible with molten sulfur, thermo-fluidic characterization and design investigation of molten sulfur TES using physics-based simulation tools validated using data from lab prototype testing, techno- economic evaluation to establish the system lifetime cost, and pilot-scale testing of the molten sulfur TES for performance verification. The objectives of the project are: Budget Period 1 1. Identify, recruit and engage with thermal energy storage, cost modeling and corrosion experts and solar thermal providers for independent review of the research and development activities. 2. Develop an economic decision-making modeling and preliminary molten sulfur TES cost modeling tool informed by fabrication partner and reviewed by experts to determine the cost targets for thermal energy storage development. 3. Characterize the corrosion rates and mechanical durability of various alloys compatible with molten sulfur through thermal cyclic tests to identify the suitable containment material(s) that meets the cost target for sulfur containment vessel. 4. Identify and engage with potential host site partners for pilot prototype testing, and interact with solar thermal providers, stakeholders to evaluate and understand the Page 9 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. critical parameters to be considered in the design of molten sulfur TES that will feed into the activities planned for budget period 2. Budget Period 2 5. Characterize the performance of the molten sulfur TES for various operation modes through experimental testing of the lab prototype unit. 6. Develop a computational model that captures the sulfur thermo-fluidic behavior validated using the data obtained from lab prototype testing and utilize it to design the molten sulfur TES for pilot testing. 7. Develop a reduced order performance model of the molten sulfur TES and cost model reviewed by experts for robust design optimization to identify design configuration that meets the cost target for internal heat exchanger geometry. 8. Finalize the pilot design and drawings of molten sulfur TES reviewed by experts for fabrication and obtain a signed agreement with one of the host sites for pilot testing. Budget Period 3 9. Pilot scale fabrication, testing and characterization of the molten sulfur TES performance for various operation modes pertinent to integration with concentrated solar thermal for industrial process heat applications. 10. Validate the performance modeling and design tools based on measurements from the pilot-scale unit testing and use it in conjunction with cost modeling tool to identify a realistic pathway to achieve the storage cost target at scale for commercial success. 11.
